title: Behavioral Integrity Verification for AI Agent Skills
abstract: arXiv:2605.11770v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Agent skills extend LLM agents with privileged third-party capabilities such as filesystem access, credentials, network calls, and shell execution. Existing safety work catches malicious prompts and risky runtime actions, but the skill artifact itself goes unverified. We formalize this as the behavioral integrity verification (BIV) problem: a typed set comparison between declared and actual capabilities over a shared taxonomy that bridges code, instructions, and metadata. The BIV framework instantiates this comparison by pairing deterministic code analysis with LLM-assisted capability extraction. The resulting structured evidence supports three downstream analyses: deviation taxonomy, root-cause classification, and malicious-skill detection. translated_title: AI智能体技能的行为完整性验证
translated_abstract: 智能体技能通过赋予大语言模型（LLM）智能体特权第三方能力（如文件系统访问、凭证、网络调用和shell执行）来扩展其功能。现有的安全工作能够捕获恶意提示和危险的运行时操作，但技能工件本身却未经验证。我们将此问题形式化为行为完整性验证问题：在一个连接代码、指令和元数据的共享分类体系上，对声明能力与实际能力进行类型化集合比较。BIV框架通过将确定性代码分析与LLM辅助的能力提取相结合来实现这一比较。所产生的结构化证据支持三种下游分析：偏差分类、根因分类和恶意技能检测。在来自OpenClaw注册表的49,943个技能上，偏差分类揭示了一种普遍存在的描述与实现之间的差距：80.0%的技能在分类体系中至少存在一处偏差，其中四个（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出行为完整性验证（BIV）框架，通过将确定性代码分析与LLM辅助能力提取相结合，对智能体技能的声明能力与实际能力进行类型化集合比较，并在49,943个OpenClaw技能上发现80%的技能存在描述与实现之间的偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Behavioral Integrity Verification (BIV) framework, which performs a typed set comparison between declared and actual capabilities of agent skills by pairing deterministic code analysis with LLM-assisted capability extraction, revealing that 80% of 49,943 OpenClaw registry skills exhibit description-implementation deviations.
